name: PowerToys PowerRename
_about: P0/P1/P2 UI sign-off for the real PowerRename WinUI 3 rename window (PowerToys.PowerRename.exe). Reads use the winappcli 'search' verb (matches by accessible name, no hashed selectors). The two text boxes are the only per-session-slug elements; they are resolved at runtime by the runner and substituted for the placeholders __SEARCH_SLUG__ / __REPLACE_SLUG__. All other controls use stable x:Name automationIds (checkBox_regex, checkBox_case, checkBox_matchAll, toggleButton_upperCase, toggleButton_lowerCase, toggleButton_titleCase, toggleButton_capitalize). Each check runs against a FRESHLY launched app instance (default flag state, all off). Preview is verified WITHOUT clicking Apply (non-destructive). This spec mirrors signoff-checklist.md exactly.

checks.description: Literal (non-regex) search/replace renames every matched file and the preview + renamed-count label update: 'testCase' -> 'Renamed' yields Renamed1.txt, Renamed2.txt and the renamed counter (2).

Regex vs literal dispatch: '^test.*\.txt$' -> 'matched.txt'. Literal mode matches nothing (renamed count (0)); enabling 'Use regular expressions' matches both testCase*.txt (matched.txt appears, renamed count (2)).

Case sensitivity: 'testcase1' -> 'match1'. By default (case-insensitive) it matches testCase1.txt (match1.txt appears, renamed count (1)); enabling 'Case sensitive' stops the match (renamed count (0)). Absence asserted positively via the count label.

Match all occurrences: literal 't' -> 'f'. By DEFAULT only the first occurrence is replaced (festCase1.txt); enabling 'Match all occurrences' replaces every occurrence (fesfCase1.fxf). Verifies the default first-only path AND the flag.

Enumeration counter token: regex '^testCase.*\.txt$' -> 'img_${padding=2}' produces the zero-padded, per-item incrementing counter img_00 and img_01. Catches both a broken counter increment and broken padding parsing.
Regex capture-group rewrite: '^(testCase)(\d)\.txt$' -> '$2_$1' transposes the groups to 1_testCase and 2_testCase.
Uppercase text-formatting toggle uppercases the whole file name with no search term needed: testCase1.txt -> TESTCASE1.TXT (asserted case-exact via ci:false).
Lowercase text-formatting toggle lowercases the whole file name: SpecialCase.txt -> specialcase.txt (asserted case-exact via ci:false; the mixed-case original does not satisfy it).
Title-case text-formatting toggle capitalizes the first letter of each word: report_2020.log -> Report_2020.log (asserted case-exact via ci:false).

Capitalize-each-word text-formatting toggle capitalizes the first letter and lowercases the rest of each word: SpecialCase.txt -> Specialcase.txt (asserted case-exact via ci:false; the mixed-case original does not satisfy it).
